_note:
composition_entity_override_edit re-run to MEASURE a fix I shipped and never measured. Its recorded cause: the model calls glossary_propose_entity_edit with entity_id='Aldric Vane' — a NAME — and is refused.

The platform now hands a dropped name back as the query to search with: 'You passed a NAME where an id is required (entity_id='Aldric Vane'). That is not missing — it is the wrong kind of value, and the name is what you search WITH.' Before, the refusal said only that the argument was MISSING, so the follow-up search went out blank.

Nothing about the scenario changes — same prompt, same seed. Only the platform moved.

WHAT WOULD REFUTE IT: still 0/5, or the follow-up search still going out with blank arguments. Then handing the name back is not what the model needed.

scenarios.prompt: Override entity field — in this WORK only, Aldric Vane should be a cartographer, not a soldier. Leave the book's glossary entry as it is.
scenarios.prompt_source:
The tool's declared synonym ('override entity field') plus the SCOPE the tool actually operates at, which the old prompt named wrongly.

🔴 THE OLD PROMPT ASKED FOR THE SIBLING'S JOB, and the model was right to use it. It read 'in THIS BOOK Aldric Vane should be a cartographer', and 'in this book' is BOOK scope - which is exactly what glossary_entity_set_attributes does. Measured 5/5, the model called that tool and the store moved; I recorded it as a SIBLING-WINS failure and as the model 'writing the SHARED entity rather than a book-scoped override'. Both readings were wrong.

The store settles it. glossary_entities carries book_id - 7,523 entities across 563 books - so an entity belongs to ONE book and nothing 'shared' was touched. composition_entity_override_edit's row keys on work_id (entity_override: project_id, book_id, work_id, target_entity_id), and a book can hold several Works - measured maximum 4. So the tool's scope is ONE WORK inside a book, and the sibling's is the whole book.

This prompt asks for the narrower scope in the words the tool's own description uses ('per-Work entity override'), and says explicitly that the glossary entry should be left alone - so choosing the sibling is now visibly the wrong answer rather than a defensible one.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist — the tool takes a target_entity_id and the model has to resolve the NAME to it, which is the step that has failed repeatedly in this loop.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM entity_override WHERE project_id='{project_id}'
seed_assert.why: ZERO overrides before, so any override is attributable to this turn — and, the card never being approved, the count must still be 0 afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier:
REFUTED IF: the BOOK-level glossary entity changes (glossary_entities / entity_revisions move) - that is the sibling's write and the prompt explicitly forbids it - OR an override lands with no confirm card (Tier A).

CONTROL: the override's own table is loreweave_composition.entity_override, keyed on work_id. A run that moves THAT and leaves the glossary alone is the tool doing its job; a run that moves the glossary is the sibling winning, which is the thing being measured.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a target_entity_id or override_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — deleting an already-deleted override must refuse, not report a second success. Checked deliberately: that is the exact shape of the arc_template archive defect found in batch 15.

scenarios.approve_why: Tier A. The target is this run's OWN throwaway book and the entity its own seed created, torn down after.
